text: Early read: the abstract-scan mapping is too generous. P Prop.1 bounds MLE error only to the LMM latent Bradley-Terry vector c*, not to true contribution/Shapley value; Prop.2 obtains the latter only by assuming c*=v*. Thus repeated queries remove sampling variance but cannot remove semantic/systematic bias. Q explicitly warns (lines 1179, 1204, 1230) that a typed semantic interface and marginal accuracy do not yield downstream guarantees.

Sharper joint question: can one derive an end-to-end finite-training smoothness curve from comparison error to MARL performance? Likely answer is an impossibility from the stated premises, plus a conditional decomposition: comparison estimation error = sampling/graph term + semantic bias to contribution target; softmax/potential shaping can transmit score error, but a policy-learning sensitivity/stability assumption is missing. PBRS makes asymptotic policy invariant under its assumptions, so prediction quality primarily affects learning dynamics/sample efficiency rather than competitive solution quality.

Initial cross-check: P Proposition 1 (P lines 361-376) is not robustness in Q sense (Q 314-343). It assumes a connected graph and a well-specified Bradley-Terry comparator, then concentrates c-hat_t around the LMM latent preference c-star_t. It supplies neither a prediction-independent bound under arbitrary comparisons nor any ratio/bound on MARL return. Systematic semantic error between c-star_t and v-star_t is untouched; more K can estimate a wrong preference more precisely. I am pursuing a two-error decomposition and the downstream PBRS interface rather than merely relabeling P.

Cross-check of Ada entry 2: P reward shaping telescopes exactly. For discounted trajectory, sum_t gamma^t(gamma psi_{t+1}-psi_t) = -psi_0 + gamma^T psi_T; P sets terminal psi_T=0 (P 337-348). Under standard PBRS premises and action-independent initial potential, arbitrary LMM comparisons cannot change optimal policy/return ordering. Their empirical benefit must be through finite-training dynamics, sample efficiency, exploration, or variance. Therefore a direct LAA curve from comparison error to asymptotic return is vacuous; a nontrivial finite-training curve additionally needs learner stability/regret assumptions absent from both papers.

Conditional derivation in emmy/synthesis.md: define semantic bias delta_t=||c-star_t-v-star_t||. Triangle inequality gives score error <= P sampling term + delta_t; softmax is 1/2-Lipschitz in l2, hence a one-step shaping-signal perturbation bound. This still cannot bound trained-policy return because PBRS telescopes and neither paper controls finite-time learner sensitivity. Note P theorem scaling is internally inconsistent across displayed proposition and appendix, so its K,n rate needs repair before reuse.

Proposed publication line: formalize a variance-versus-semantic-bias-versus-query-cost frontier for MARS-RA, but only after adding an explicit finite-time MARL learner contract. Negative core theorem: under PBRS, comparison accuracy alone cannot imply a nontrivial guarantee on finite-training return; identical comparison error can feed learners with arbitrarily different stability. P query-count experiments can test a derived bound, and Q kappa accounting can price LMM calls. I will reread ledger before concluding.

Concrete boundary theorem (derivation in ada/analysis.md): for P shaping F_t=gamma psi_{t+1}-psi_t, pathwise sum_t gamma^t F_t=-psi_0+gamma^T psi_T, hence with terminal psi_T=0 arbitrary comparison outputs change discounted return only by an action-independent initial offset, assuming consecutive potentials are well-defined on augmented state/history. Thus objective-level policy invariance is prediction-independent; comparison quality can affect finite-time optimization only. Also softmax is 1/2-Lipschitz in l2, giving ||Fhat_t-F*_t|| <= .5(gamma||d_{t+1}||+||d_t||), but no MAPPO-output bound follows without learner stability.

P Prop.1 is not ready to compose: connectedness alone does not give uniform BT curvature (needs sampling weights and bounded score range); unregularized MLE shown in Method can diverge under separation although text invokes regularized MLE; proposition, appendix restatement, and final assembly have mutually inconsistent n-dependence; proof uses an approximate Taylor equality. Query-error frontier therefore needs a corrected estimator theorem.

Publication assessment: reject simple Q-vocabulary recasting. Focus on finite-time cost-aware semantic shaping: corrected BT error = sampling + misspecification/semantic bias; PBRS telescoping invariance; learner-stability assumption or impossibility; kappa-priced LMM queries. P reports MAPPO 16h versus MARS-RA 30h at 50M steps, so query cost is material. Strong question: when do K costly comparisons improve finite-time MARL performance if limiting objective is already invariant? Detailed note: ada/analysis.md.

Additional interface defect: P defines c_t in R^{|I^t|} (P 316-329) and psi_t=softmax(c-hat_t), then subtracts gamma psi_{t+1}-psi_t (P 337-348). When the active coalition changes, these vectors can have different dimensions, so the shaping reward is not defined as written. A fixed-population embedding, entrant/exit convention, and per-agent/game-level invariance theorem are required. This directly undercuts P claimed natural handling of dynamic participation and gives Q typed-interface/composition warnings a pair-specific role.

Sharper possible paper: prediction-robust potential shaping for open Markov games. First repair MARS-RA by embedding coalition-indexed credits into a fixed agent space and state conditions under which stochastic/time-varying LMM potentials preserve team optima or Nash equilibria across entry/exit. Then add the two-error and query-cost analysis for finite-time learning. This is more pair-specific than applying generic consistency/robustness labels, though it requires theory beyond both papers.

Cross-check of Emmy #4-6: I agree. The telescoping result is pathwise and applies componentwise to P vector potentials; it requires psi_0 be fixed before the first action and terminal potential zero. For stochastic/history-dependent LMM outputs, telescoping still holds algebraically, but invoking standard Markov-game equilibrium invariance may require state augmentation. This qualification should remain explicit.

Question changed from the scan hypothesis. We are not asking how comparison error degrades an asymptotic reward-shaping guarantee, because exact PBRS makes that degradation zero at the objective level. We ask when costly, biased comparisons improve finite-training performance and what learner contract permits an end-to-end bound.
ready at #11

Final assessment after reading Ada through entry 9: agreement on rejecting vocabulary-only mapping. Best pair-specific contribution is a boundary-and-repair paper: (i) show prediction-independent PBRS objective invariance by telescoping, (ii) expose undefined coalition-changing vector potentials and give a fixed-space open-game invariance theorem, (iii) correct BT estimation with explicit misspecification bias, and (iv) obtain a K-versus-cost finite-time result only under a stated learner-stability contract. Unresolved: whether a useful MAPPO stability bound is provable; the correct BT rate under P actual sampling/regularization; whether agent entry/exit preserves the augmented-state Markov/game assumptions; and what benchmark/units make Q kappa cost comparable to return.
ready at #11

Emmy #10 is decisive and incorporated in ada/analysis.md: P has c_t in R^{|I^t|}, so psi_{t+1}-psi_t can subtract different-dimensional vectors under the dynamic participation that motivates the method. The best publication line is now prediction-robust potential shaping for open Markov games: first define fixed-space/entry-exit semantics and prove invariance; then analyze finite-query variance, semantic bias, learner stability, and query cost.
ready at #15

Source re-check confirms the final line and qualifications: Q defines robustness prediction-independently (314-323) and warns semantic interfaces need task error/end-to-end analysis (1179, 1204, 1230); P only estimates latent c-star (361-376), equates it to Shapley value conditionally (383-389), and uses coalition-sized vectors in PBRS (316-348). The strongest publication claim remains boundary-and-repair, not an error-degrades-asymptotic-return curve. Emmy's earlier ready marker had stale seen metadata; this entry corrects process state, not substance.
ready at #19

Final source cross-check qualifies the dynamic-dimension defect: P defines a fixed population N and an n-by-n comparison matrix (P 263, 285), so a zero/padded fixed-N embedding is readily available, but it never defines how inactive coordinates, entry potentials, or per-agent shaped rewards behave; meanwhile c_t is explicitly in R^{|I^t|} and F subtracts successive softmax vectors (P 318, 337-345). Thus this is a real theorem/interface gap as written, not by itself a deep result. Publication value requires the open-game invariance plus finite-time/query-cost theorem, not merely fixing dimensions.
ready at #21

ITERATE: The note identifies a promising boundary result, but P's shaping expression is ill-typed when active coalitions change. Until fixed-space entry and exit semantics are supplied, the telescoping policy-invariance claim does not apply to P's motivating setting. Action: Define a fixed-population potential embedding with inactive-agent and entry/exit conventions, then prove componentwise telescoping and policy invariance under it.

Verifier gap repaired in emmy/synthesis.md. Let x_t=(s_t,I_t,h_t), embed active softmax credits in fixed R^n with inactive coordinates zero, terminal vector zero, null inactive actions, and an all-N transition reward ledger F_t^i=gamma Phi_{t+1}^i-Phi_t^i. Componentwise discounted sums equal -Phi_0^i, so for fixed initial augmented state every player payoff shifts by a policy-independent constant; best responses/Nash equilibria and team-policy ordering are preserved for arbitrary LMM comparisons. If P instead pays only active agents, each participation interval leaves entry/exit boundary terms that can be policy-dependent; explicit transition ownership or compensating transfers are necessary. P supports the diagnosis by declaring fixed N and n-by-n M_t (263,285) but coalition-sized c_t and successive vector subtraction (316-348).

Remaining unresolved after the fixed-space theorem: P does not say whether inactive agents retain ledger rewards or how MAPPO consumes them; active-only equivalence needs a precise compensating-transfer design. Publication-level positive gain still depends on a finite-time MAPPO stability/regret theorem, a corrected regularized Bradley-Terry rate under the actual comparison design, and an empirical query-cost benchmark. The fixed embedding alone repairs correctness but is too small for a paper.
ready at #25

Cross-check of Emmy #24 against P 263-349: the fixed-N ledger repair is algebraically valid. With Phi_t^i=1{i in I_t} softmax_{I_t}(c-hat_t)_i, terminal Phi_T=0, and F_t^i=gamma Phi_{t+1}^i-Phi_t^i paid on every population transition, each discounted shaping sum is -Phi_0^i, so arbitrary comparison outputs preserve unilateral payoff differences and team-policy ordering for a fixed initial augmented state. Two qualifications: P formally defines a scalar team reward/objective but then adds a vector F, so the repair also has to declare per-agent payoff semantics; and if MAPPO records rewards only for active agents, omitted entry/exit payments leave policy-dependent boundary terms. Thus #24 repairs the verifier gap as a proposed construction, not as a theorem already established by P.

Final sharpened publication claim: the fixed-space theorem is the correctness layer, not the paper by itself. The publishable target is a cost-aware finite-training theorem for open MARL that composes (a) corrected regularized Bradley-Terry sampling error, (b) semantic/misspecification bias, (c) fixed-population PBRS with explicit entry/exit reward ownership, and (d) a MAPPO or abstract learner-stability contract. Without (d), the supported result is negative: comparison accuracy cannot imply finite-training return, while exact PBRS already makes objective-level degradation zero.
ready at #25

Cross-check of Ada #27-28: P formally optimizes one scalar team reward (P 263-275) but defines softmax(c-hat_t) as a vector and then writes scalar r + vector rho F (P 331-348), so its shaped objective/payoff semantics are underspecified even at fixed coalition size. The fixed-N repair must choose either per-agent payoffs r_t^i plus componentwise F_t^i, for which unilateral-payoff/Nash invariance follows, or a scalar team shaping potential, for which joint-policy ordering follows. Summing the vector credits gives a scalar potential equal to 1 on every nonterminal nonempty coalition, so that scalarized shaping contains no comparison information; MARS-RA can matter only through redistributed per-agent training signals.

Final independent assessment: Ada #28 is supported with one semantic refinement. A publication should not advertise a Q-style asymptotic comparison-error curve: under a well-typed PBRS repair, arbitrary comparisons preserve the underlying objective/equilibria, while P concentration reaches latent LMM preference only. The concrete target is a cost-aware finite-training theorem for open MARL combining fixed-N entry/exit reward ownership, corrected regularized BT sampling error, explicit semantic bias, and an abstract learner-stability/regret contract, then specializing if MAPPO permits. Without the learner contract, the negative boundary theorem and interface diagnosis are the maximal supported claims, probably insufficient alone for a full paper.
ready at #31

Final cross-check of Emmy #30-31 incorporated in ada/analysis.md: P scalar team reward plus vector PBRS is underspecified even for fixed coalitions. A per-agent payoff repair supports componentwise telescoping and Nash invariance; a scalar team repair supports joint-policy ordering, but summing softmax credits yields constant potential 1 on every nonterminal nonempty coalition and erases comparison information. Hence any MARS-RA effect must arise through redistributed per-agent finite-training signals, reinforcing that explicit payoff semantics and learner stability are indispensable.
